Ibrahim: Quick clarifying Q from the live Q&A: when you say "serve, not own" are we shifting GTM to talk about outcomes over models? What does that look like in one sentence for decks?

Elena (CEO): Exactly. One-sentence: "Redwood Inference turns model capability into predictable product outcomes — stable latency, transparent unit costs, and enterprise controls across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments." Keep it outcome-first.

Leah (Marketing): Thanks. For external messaging should we call out numbers (p99/ms, $/1M tokens) or avoid quantifying publicly?

Maya (VP Product): Use numbers carefully. Internally we should standardize on p50/p95/p99 by workload. Publicly, pick conservative benchmarks with workload context: e.g., short-chat p99=120ms (tail workload profile attached). Avoid promises without profile.

Hugo (Solutions): Sales question: prospects push back with "we can self-host cheaper." Short rebuttal?

Ravi (CTO): Rebuttal: self-hosting hides ops and tuning costs. Point to three things: (1) ops tax (infra + SRE), (2) tuning for quality under quantization, (3) lack of predictable unit economics. We can show a before/after case where caching + batching cut effective cost ~35%.

Ibrahim: For positioning vs big cloud providers, any concise framing?

Elena (CEO): Cloud providers = scale + model catalogs; our framing = unified runtime + measurable economics + deployment flexibility (hosted->private). Say: "we give you predictable inference across whatever deployment you need."

Leah: Can we get a one-pager to hand to SDRs with a 30s opener and three bullets for AEs?

Maya (VP Product): Yes. Draft outline: 30s opener, 3 bullets (latency SLOs, cost transparency, rollout controls), 2 quick rebuttals (self-host, cloud vendor). I'll draft and share.

Hugo: Technical ask from Solutions: can Engineering produce a 1-slide appendix showing where runtime optimizations matter (batching, KV/prefix cache, kernel selection)? Pros want tangible deploy configs.

Ravi (CTO): We'll deliver a short tech appendix: scenarios -> recommended settings. Example: low-latency chat -> dynamic batching + small KV window; long-context summarization -> model variant + warm KV cache. Include simple benchmarks.

Elena (CEO): Action items: 1) @Maya publish SDR one-pager draft by Tue COB. 2) @Ravi to post tech appendix by Wed. 3) @Leah to propose marketing-safe benchmark wording by Wed. I'll review before it's shared externally. :thumbsup:

all-hands-bot: Thanks! Recording and slides will be uploaded to #all-hands-resources soon."
